title: Flame Extinguishment Experiment - 2
platform: International Space Station (Combustion Integrated Rack, Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus)
summary: Isolated and paired fuel droplets (1.5-5 mm; pure alkanes, alcohols and bi-component mixtures) were ignited aboard the ISS in O2/N2 or O2/He at 0.5-3 atm and 17-30% O2 to measure burning and flame extinction without buoyancy and benchmark droplet combustion models.

tests.notes: Source row is a test-matrix envelope, not a single run: initial droplet diameter 1.5-5 mm (not a thickness, so thickness_mm = null); ambient O2/N2 or O2/He at 25 C. O2 mole fraction listed as 0.17, 0.21, 0.25, 0.30 -> midpoint 23.5% with range [17, 30]. Pressure listed as 0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0 or 3.0 atm (no range field in contract) -> midpoint 1.75 atm = 177.3 kPa. Flow velocity 0.1-5 cm/s -> midpoint 2.55 cm/s; per Approach, flow comes from translating the droplet only in some tests, others are quiescent, so flow_direction = mixed. Outcome not reported in the table; set to partial_burn because FLEX-2 studies flame extinction at finite droplet diameter (radiative / cool-flame extinction), but actual outcome varies per run.
